FAQ

### Questions before we start

Straight answers on scope, pricing, and how engagements run.

Project work is fixed-fee, quoted after the discovery call. Ongoing performance and automation retainers are monthly, scoped to the channels and hours involved. You always know the number before any work starts, with no percentage-of-spend surprises.

Thirty minutes. You describe the business, the goal, and what you've tried. I ask questions, look at what you share, and tell you honestly whether I can help. If I can, you get a scoped proposal. If not, I'll point you somewhere useful.

I do. There's no account-manager layer or outsourced pod. You work directly with the person responsible for the result.

A shared Slack or WhatsApp channel for the day-to-day, a scheduled monthly review call, and email for anything formal. You talk to me directly.

No hard number, but paid campaigns need enough budget to generate useful data, typically a few hundred dollars a month at minimum. On the call I'll tell you whether your budget fits your goal.

Research takes about a week. Website builds run two to six weeks. Paid campaigns show meaningful data within four to six weeks and stabilise over a quarter. Anyone promising results in a week is guessing.

Google, Meta (Facebook and Instagram), LinkedIn, TikTok, Snapchat, Microsoft, and Amazon. Where to spend comes from where your buyers are, not from a preference for any platform.

Both. I build on Shopify, WordPress, Wix Studio, Webflow, and custom stacks. Because I also run campaigns, everything is built to convert and to measure.

Practical workflows: leads scored and routed in minutes, follow-ups that send themselves, WhatsApp answered out of hours, and reports that build themselves. No experimental tools in production.

Campaign optimisation, budget management, creative and copy iterations, landing page recommendations, tracking maintenance, and a monthly report focused on revenue. You keep full ownership and admin access.

Revenue metrics agreed up front: qualified leads, CAC, ROAS, and pipeline contribution, pulled from your CRM and analytics, not screenshots of ad dashboards.

Every build ships with documentation and a handover call. Websites include 30 days of post-launch fixes. After that, move to a retainer or engage ad-hoc. Nothing is locked in.

# About Sushant Rana — Growth Consultant, Chandigarh

About us

## Sushant Rana, building revenue systems since 2017

I'm Sushant Rana, a project manager and business growth consultant based in Chandigarh, India. I started doing digital marketing in 2017, first learning under someone else while freelancing, then through full-time roles. I still hold a full-time job today, and alongside it I consult and deliver services independently under my own company, Sushant Rana.

That mix is deliberate. The job keeps me shipping large projects with real teams and real budgets every week. The consulting keeps me close to owners who need a revenue system, not a vendor. In between, I have delivered work for nine client brands across five countries, and I write about how those systems are built in my articles on revenue systems and lead quality.
Book a free consultation

The journey

### From freelancer to project manager

012017

#### Learning the craft

Started digital marketing under a mentor and took my first freelance projects on the side. Small budgets, real accountability, and the fastest way to learn what actually moves a number.

02October 2018 – March 2025

#### Digital Marketing Manager, House Of Web

Six and a half years running campaigns, websites and tracking for clients across four markets. Paid media, SEO, CRO, and the reporting that keeps all three honest.

03March 2025 – present

#### Project Manager

Leading cross-functional delivery across performance marketing, web development and CRM operations, turning business requirements into systems that ship on time.

04Today

#### Consulting as Sushant Rana

Alongside the job, I consult and deliver services independently under my own company, Sushant Rana. Senior-led engagements only, so the person you talk to is the person doing the work.

Client work

### Brands I have worked with

Nine businesses across renovation, overseas education, ecommerce, martial arts, legal services and fire safety engineering, in India, the UAE, Canada, Switzerland and the United States. Each one bought a different service, from a single ad account to a full website and revenue system.

What we do

### Six disciplines, one engine

Most businesses buy these separately and wonder why nothing compounds. Performance marketing, CRM automation and the website only work together when one person owns the whole chain from click to closed deal. These are the same six disciplines behind the revenue systems I build for clients.

#### Performance marketing

Google Ads and Meta Ads built around pipeline, not impressions.

#### CRM and marketing automation

Zoho CRM, GoHighLevel and HubSpot: pipelines, workflows, and email, SMS and WhatsApp nurture.

#### Sales funnel strategy

Landing pages, offers and follow-up sequences that turn traffic into booked calls.

#### Website development

WordPress, Elementor and Shopify builds tuned for speed and conversion.

#### Tracking and reporting

Google Tag Manager and GA4 set up so every rupee is traceable to a result.

#### SEO and conversion rate optimisation

Organic visibility and page-level testing compounding on top of paid.

FAQ

### Questions about working with me

#### Who is Sushant Rana?

Sushant Rana is a Project Manager and Business Growth Consultant based in India. He has been working in performance marketing since 2017, specializing in paid advertising, growth strategy, funnels, CRM, automation, and digital marketing. He currently works as a Project Manager while independently consulting businesses under his own brand, Sushant Rana.

#### Is the first consultation free?

Yes. The first consultation is a free 30-minute call. You describe the business, the goal and what you have already tried; Sushant asks questions and tells you honestly whether he can help. There is no charge and no obligation for that call.

#### How do I book a free consultation and when are slots available?

Book through the consultation form on sushantrana.com or by emailing me@sushantrana.com. Calls run on weekday evenings India time and on weekends, which is what makes them workable for clients in Canada, Switzerland and the United States as well as India. You get a confirmed slot rather than a queue.

#### What does Sushant Rana charge for consulting?

The first 30-minute consultation is free. After that, project work is quoted as a fixed fee once the scope is clear, and ongoing performance marketing, SEO or automation work is a monthly retainer scoped to the channels involved. You always know the number before any work starts, and there is no percentage-of-ad-spend billing.

#### Which types of businesses does he consult?

Businesses that sell a considered purchase and need a repeatable enquiry pipeline: home renovation and contracting, overseas education consultants, aviation and career training institutes, D2C ecommerce brands, fitness and martial arts academies, real estate, law firms and professional services, and fire safety engineering and B2B suppliers. Those are the categories in the client work above, not a wish list.

#### Will he consult if a business is already working with another agency?

Yes. Plenty of engagements start while an agency is already running the ad accounts. In that case the work is usually an audit and a second opinion: what the current setup is doing well, what is leaking budget, and what would have to change. There is no requirement to fire anyone to have the conversation.

#### What services does Sushant Rana offer?

Performance marketing on Google Ads and Meta Ads, CRM setup and marketing automation on Zoho, HubSpot and GoHighLevel, sales funnel strategy, WordPress and Shopify website development, conversion tracking with Google Tag Manager and GA4, SEO, and conversion rate optimisation.

#### Which clients has Sushant Rana worked with?

Yalla Renovation, 4S Study Abroad, Achievers Perfect Career Institute (APCI), OurKnots, Warrior's Cove, Bazayan.ch, Touch Abroad, Trust Legal and Elixir Engineering, across India, the UAE, Canada, Switzerland and the United States.

#### How many years of digital marketing experience does he have?

Since 2017. He freelanced first while learning under a mentor, then spent six and a half years in-house as Digital Marketing Manager at House Of Web, and since March 2025 as a Project Manager.

#### Does he work with clients outside India?

Yes. Current and past engagements include Warrior's Cove in Minnesota, USA, Touch Abroad in Mississauga, Canada, Bazayan.ch in Switzerland, and Yalla Renovation and 4S Study Abroad in Dubai, UAE, alongside Indian clients in Chandigarh Tricity and across North India.

#### Is he available for freelance and consulting work alongside a full-time job?

Yes. He holds a full-time project management role and takes on consulting and service engagements independently under his own brand, Sushant Rana. Every engagement is senior-led, so the person on the call is the person doing the work.

#### How long before a new engagement shows results?

Research takes about a week. Website builds run two to six weeks. Paid campaigns produce meaningful data in four to six weeks and stabilise over a quarter. SEO is slower, so expect movement over three to six months. Anyone promising rankings or ROAS in a week is guessing.

#### Who owns the ad accounts, website and data?

You do. Accounts, domains, CRM and analytics stay in your name with full admin access throughout the engagement and after it ends. Nothing is held hostage as a retention tactic.

### Let's build a system that keeps growing.

One call. One engine. Strategy, ads, automation, and site, aligned to your revenue goal.

Common questions

### Questions about my services

#### Which service should I start with?

It depends on where your leads are leaking. If people cannot find you, start with SEO or Google Ads. If they find you but do not enquire, fix the website or landing page first. If enquiries come in but are not followed up, start with the CRM. On a free strategy call I look at your setup and tell you where to start.

#### Can you run several of these services together?

Yes. Most clients use more than one, for example ads with a landing page, or ads connected to a CRM. One person owning the whole system means nothing falls between two vendors.

#### Will I work with you directly?

Yes. You talk to the same person who plans and runs the work, from the first call to the results.

#### Do you work with businesses outside India?

Yes. I work from Chandigarh, India, with clients across India, the UAE, the USA, Canada and Australia, on Google Meet and WhatsApp.

#### Is the strategy call free?

Yes. The strategy call is free, takes 30 minutes on Google Meet, and comes with no obligation to work together.

### Not sure where to start?

Tell me about your business and I will suggest the service that fits, or a mix of them.

Common questions

### Shopify store development questions, answered

Timelines, pricing, ownership, migrations and support. If yours is not here, ask me on the call.

#### How long does a Shopify store build take?

Most builds take four to six weeks: discovery in week one, design by week two, development through week five, then testing and launch in week six. You get a dated schedule before anything is agreed.

#### What does the price cover?

Scoping, design, hand written development, two revision rounds, the responsive build, browser and device testing, and thirty days of support after launch. Nothing is added to the invoice later.

#### Who owns the code and the design files?

You do, completely. Source files, design assets and the theme are handed over when the project closes. There is no licence to renew and no vendor to stay tied to.

#### How many revision rounds are included?

Two rounds come as standard. Further rounds are available at a flat hourly rate, though most projects are settled after the first.

#### What if I need changes once the store is live?

The first thirty days cover fixes and small adjustments at no cost. Beyond that we work either on a monthly retainer or task by task, whichever suits you.

#### How does payment work?

Half to begin and half on delivery is the usual arrangement. Longer projects can be split across milestones instead. Bank transfer and UPI both work for clients in India.

#### Will you sign an NDA?

Yes. Send yours across before we talk specifics, or use ours if that is easier.

#### Can I see examples of stores you have built?

Yes. On the discovery call we walk you through relevant projects and live links, so you can judge the work rather than take our word for it.

#### How quickly do you respond to support requests?

You will hear back within a few working hours, and most issues are resolved inside a day or two. Anything breaking on a live storefront is handled the same day.

#### Will my existing apps still work?

Yes. The usual ecommerce stack, including Klaviyo, ReCharge, Yotpo, Judge.me, Gorgias and the common shipping tools, is carried across and reconfigured properly.

#### What if I am unhappy with the result?

Then it is not finished. We would rather return to the drawing board than hand over a storefront you would hesitate to share.

#### Do you handle putting the store live?

Yes. The new theme goes up as a duplicate for review first, then goes live while you watch, and we stay reachable for the following day.

#### How will we communicate during the project?

Short written updates on WhatsApp or Slack, a call whenever a decision needs one, and one shared document holding the brief, the mockups and every decision made.

#### What do you need from me to start?

Your current store link if there is one, any brand guidelines, a few reference sites you admire, and a short note on what the store has to achieve. A structured questionnaire follows kickoff.

#### Do you offer ongoing support after the first month?

Yes. Monthly retainers cover continued optimisation, design updates, app work and fixes for store owners who would rather not manage it themselves.

#### Will my store look different from other Shopify sites?

Yes. Nothing is reused between clients. Wireframes start from your catalogue and your customers, so the finished storefront belongs to your brand alone. Why most Shopify stores look alike, and how to avoid it

#### Can I edit the content myself afterwards?

Yes. Every section is exposed in the Shopify theme editor, so wording, images, colours and buttons can all be changed without touching code.

#### What if I want to add products or new sections later?

The store is built on Online Store 2.0 with reusable sections, so you can add products, collections and pages yourself. Bring us back only when you want something genuinely new built.

#### Can you move my products across from another platform?

Yes. Products, customer records, order history, redirects and the SEO groundwork all come across, which is what keeps your existing rankings intact through the move.

#### Which apps will I actually need?

Only the ones that earn their place. We suggest a short, deliberate stack for reviews, email and retention, set it up correctly, and leave the rest out so the store stays fast.

Tell me what you sell and where you want the business to be in a year. I will come back with a plan, a price and a launch date.

Common questions

### Website maintenance questions, answered

Cost, platforms, security and how we work together. Still unsure? Ask me directly.

Ask my question

#### The basics

##### What is website maintenance?

Website maintenance is the regular work that keeps a live website secure, fast and correct: backups, software and plugin updates, security checks, bug fixes, broken link repairs and content changes. It is to a website what servicing is to a car.

##### Why does my website need a maintenance plan?

Software, plugins, browsers and search engines keep changing. Without regular care a site slows down, breaks or becomes an easy target for hackers. A plan keeps it updated, backed up and working, with someone already responsible when something goes wrong.

##### What is included in website maintenance services?

Every plan includes backups, security scans, disaster recovery, hosting and webmail support, SSL and domain monitoring, and broken link fixes. Higher plans add CMS and plugin updates, content and design changes, new pages, Search Console and Analytics setup, and malware cleanup.

##### What happens if I do not maintain my website?

Outdated plugins and themes are the most common way sites get hacked. Unmaintained sites also slow down, show errors after browser or platform updates, lose forms and payments without anyone noticing, and slowly drop in Google rankings.

##### How often should a website be maintained?

Backups and security checks should run at least monthly, and weekly for busy or ecommerce sites. Plugin and platform updates are best applied as they release, after testing. A full health check of speed, SEO and broken links every month keeps small problems small.

##### Can I maintain my website myself?

You can handle simple text changes yourself. Updates, backups, security and fixing what breaks after an update need technical knowledge and time. Most business owners find a plan costs less than the hours, and the risk, of doing it alone.

##### What is the difference between website maintenance and website support?

Maintenance is planned, preventive work like updates, backups and checks. Support is fixing a problem after it appears. Every plan here covers both, so you do not pay separately when something breaks.

#### Cost and plans

##### How much does website maintenance cost in India?

Plans start at ₹18,000 a year for 7 hours of work a month, with a 15 hour plan at ₹22,000 and a 30 hour plan at ₹44,000 a year. Clients in India pay 18% GST on top. Very large or complex sites may need a custom quote.

##### How much does website maintenance cost per month?

Billed yearly, the plans work out to roughly ₹1,500, ₹1,830 and ₹3,670 a month, depending on how many hours of work your site needs each month.

##### What is a website AMC?

AMC stands for Annual Maintenance Contract. It is a yearly agreement where one team takes care of your website's upkeep for a fixed price, instead of you paying for each fix separately. All three plans here are AMCs.

##### Which plan should I choose?

A small business site with few changes is usually fine on Essential. If you update content often or run a CMS with many plugins or apps, pick Growth. Ecommerce stores and high-traffic sites suit Complete.

##### Are hosting and domain charges included?

No. Hosting and domain renewals are paid to your provider and stay in your name. The plan covers managing them: tracking renewal dates, handling hosting issues with the provider and keeping SSL and webmail working.

#### Platforms

##### Which platforms and CMS do you maintain?

WordPress, WooCommerce, Shopify, Wix, Wix Studio, Squarespace, Webflow, Framer, Magento, BigCommerce, Joomla, Drupal, Ghost and HubSpot CMS, plus custom HTML, React and Next.js sites and sites built with AI tools.

##### Do Wix, Squarespace, Shopify or Webflow websites need maintenance?

Yes, though less of it. The platform takes care of hosting and core security, but content, SEO settings, speed, forms, integrations, apps, domains and broken links are still yours to look after. Those are exactly what the plans cover.

##### What does WordPress maintenance include?

Core, theme and plugin updates tested before they go live, PHP version checks, database cleanup, backups, malware scanning, speed work and fixing anything an update breaks. WordPress needs the most regular care of any CMS because of its plugins.

##### What does Shopify store maintenance include?

Theme updates, app reviews and leftover app code cleanup, product and collection uploads, speed work, broken link and image fixes, checkout and payment checks, and design changes to sections and pages.

##### Do you maintain Webflow and Framer websites?

Yes. That covers CMS collection updates, new pages built with your existing components, interaction and layout fixes on new screen sizes, form and integration checks, SEO settings and publishing changes safely.

##### Do you maintain custom HTML, React or vibe-coded websites?

Yes. Sites built by hand or with AI tools such as Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit or Cursor still need dependency and security updates, bug fixes, deployment and hosting care, and someone who can read and safely change the code.

##### Can you move my website to another platform?

Yes. Moving between platforms, for example Wix to WordPress or WooCommerce to Shopify, is a separate project. Tell me on the call and I will quote it alongside the maintenance plan.

#### Security, speed and SEO

##### What if my site gets hacked or goes down?

The site is restored from the latest clean backup, the cause is found and fixed, and security is tightened so it does not happen again. Disaster recovery is part of every plan.

##### How often is my website backed up?

Monthly on Essential, twice a month on Growth and weekly on Complete. Hosted platforms like Shopify and Wix are backed up at the content level where the platform allows it.

##### Can you make my slow website faster?

Yes. Speed work covers image compression, removing unused plugins, apps and scripts, caching, and fixing whatever the Core Web Vitals report flags. Keeping it fast after that is part of the monthly checks.

##### Does website maintenance help SEO?

Yes. Google favours fast, secure, error-free sites. Fixing broken links and 404 errors, keeping SSL valid, improving speed and watching Search Console for problems all protect the rankings you already have.

#### Working together

##### Do you maintain websites you did not build?

Yes. Every new site starts with a health check, so any existing problems are found and listed before the plan begins.

##### Will I keep ownership and admin access to my website?

Yes. Your website, domain, hosting and accounts stay in your name. I work through the access you give and you can remove it at any time.

##### How do I request changes to my website?

Send the change on WhatsApp or email with the page and what should change. It is worked into your monthly hours and you are told when it is live.

The real problem

### Why most Google Ads accounts waste money

Many business owners tell me their Google Ads just do not work. In most cases the account was set up in a rush and never fixed. The most common leaks are broken conversion tracking, no negative keywords, the wrong keyword match types and sending clicks to a weak page.

When I take over an account, I fix these problems first. Very often this alone brings down the cost per lead and starts turning a losing account into a profitable one.

Common questions

### Google Ads management questions, answered

Budgets, timelines, tracking and reporting. If yours is not here, ask me on the call.

#### What are Google Ads?

Google Ads is Google's paid advertising system. It lets your business appear at the top of Google search results, on YouTube, on Maps and across millions of websites, so you reach people who are looking for what you sell.

#### How much budget do I need for Google Ads?

It depends on your industry and your goals. Some clients start small and scale up once we see profit. On our first call I will suggest a realistic starting budget for your market so you never overspend.

#### How soon will I get leads from Google Ads?

Google Ads can bring traffic and leads within the first few days. The first few weeks are used to gather data and improve the account, so stable results usually build from the first month onwards.

#### What is the difference between Google Ads and SEO?

Google Ads brings instant paid traffic, while SEO builds free traffic slowly over time. Ads are great for fast results, and the best growth usually comes from using both together.

#### What is Quality Score and why does it matter?

Quality Score is Google's rating of how relevant your ad, keyword and landing page are. A higher score lowers your cost per click and improves your ad position, so it saves you money.

#### What are negative keywords?

Negative keywords are searches you do not want to pay for. Adding them stops your ads from showing on the wrong searches, which saves a large part of your budget.

#### Do you set up conversion tracking?

Yes, and it is one of the first things I fix. Without correct tracking you cannot know which clicks turn into leads and sales, so I set this up properly using tools like Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics 4.

#### What is Performance Max?

Performance Max is a smart Google campaign that shows your ads across all of Google from one setup. It works well when it is guided with strong data and clear goals, which is exactly what I do.

#### Do I need a CRM to run Google Ads?

You can run ads without one, but then Google only learns from form fills, good and bad alike. When your CRM sends back which leads were qualified and which became sales, Google Ads bids for more people like your real customers. I connect Zoho, HubSpot or GoHighLevel to your account, or set one up if you do not have a CRM yet.

#### Can you run Google Shopping ads for my store?

Yes. I set up your product feed and run Shopping and Performance Max campaigns that put your products in front of ready to buy shoppers and track every sale.

#### Do I need a landing page for Google Ads?

In most cases a focused landing page converts much better than a normal website page. If your page is weak I will point it out and help you improve it, because it directly affects your cost per lead.

#### Will you write the ad copy?

Yes. I write clear, benefit driven ad copy and test different versions to find the ones that bring the most clicks and conversions at the lowest cost.

#### How do you stop my budget from being wasted?

I add negative keywords, use the right match types, fix tracking, pause weak keywords and send traffic only to strong pages. These steps cut waste and lower your cost per result.

#### Can you fix my existing Google Ads account?

Yes. This is one of the most common requests I get. I audit your account, find the leaks and rebuild the parts that are holding you back.

#### Do you manage Google Ads for local businesses?

Yes. Local businesses do very well on Google Ads when campaigns are set up carefully with the right locations, keywords and call tracking.

#### What reports will I get?

You get clear monthly reports in plain language that show what you spent and what you earned back, plus updates whenever something important changes.

#### How do I get started?

Just book a free Google Ads audit using the button on this page. I will review your business and your account and show you how we can grow your leads and sales.

# Will My Shopify Store Look Different? | Sushant Rana

URL: https://sushantrana.com/blog/will-my-shopify-store-look-different/

Yes, if it is built around your brand instead of dressed up from a theme. Why Shopify stores look alike, and what it takes to make yours unmistakable.

- Home
- Blog
- Will My Store Look Different From Other Shopify Sites?

Shopify · 1 Oct 2026 · 7 min read

## Will My Store Look Different From Other Shopify Sites?

Yes, if it is built around your brand instead of dressed up from a theme. Why Shopify stores look alike, and what it takes to make yours unmistakable.

[Image: A distinctive orange and cream Shopify storefront standing out from a row of identical grey template stores]

In this article

- 01 Why so many Shopify stores look the same
- 02 What actually makes a store look like your brand
- 03 Theme, customised theme or custom build?
- 04 Will a unique design slow the store down or make it harder to edit?
- 05 How we make sure your store looks like no one else's
- 06 Questions to ask any Shopify developer before you hire

It is one of the first questions store owners ask on a discovery call, usually with a screenshot of a competitor open in another tab. They have noticed that a lot of Shopify stores feel interchangeable, and they do not want to pay for one more.

The short answer is yes, your store can look completely different from every other Shopify site, but only if it is designed around your brand, your products and your customers rather than assembled from a theme's default layout. Shopify itself does not make stores look the same. The way most stores are built does.

### Why so many Shopify stores look the same

Millions of businesses sell on Shopify, and a large share of them start from the same small pool of themes, including Dawn, the free theme every new store gets by default. A theme is a finished design with your logo dropped in. That is its whole value: it is fast and cheap because somebody else already made every decision.

The trouble is that thousands of other stores inherited the same decisions. Once you have browsed a few, the pattern is hard to unsee:

- The same homepage running order. Announcement bar, full-width slideshow, featured collection, image with text, newsletter sign-up. Change the photos and it is still the same page.
- The same product page. Gallery on the left, title, price, variant pills and an add-to-cart button on the right, with the description tucked into an accordion.
- The same app widgets. Review stars, sticky add-to-cart bars, countdown timers and pop-ups that look identical across every store that installs them.
- The same type and spacing. Default font pairings and default margins give pages the same rhythm, even when the colours change.
- The same photography. Supplier images and stock shots that a dozen other sellers are already using for the same product.

None of this is wrong. It is simply generic, and generic is expensive in ecommerce, because a shopper who cannot tell you apart from the next store has only price left to compare.

### What actually makes a store look like your brand

Changing the colours and the logo on a theme is customisation, not design. A store starts to feel like yours when the structural decisions come from your business instead of a template. In practice that means six things.

#### 1. A layout shaped by your catalogue

A brand with eight hero products needs a very different homepage from one with four thousand SKUs. When the layout starts from what you sell and how people choose it, the page stops resembling anyone else's, because nobody else has your catalogue.

#### 2. A type and colour system, not a colour swap

Typography does more for recognition than almost anything else on the page. A deliberate type pairing, a considered scale and a palette with rules about where each colour may appear give a store a voice that a recoloured theme never has.

#### 3. Art direction for photography

Consistent lighting, crops, backgrounds and props make a collection page look like one brand rather than a supplier feed. It is also the cheapest way to look premium, because it is a set of rules rather than a bigger budget.

#### 4. Custom sections built for how you sell

A size guide that lives beside the size selector, a bundle builder, an ingredient explorer, a before and after comparison. Sections designed around your buyer's actual questions are where a store moves from looking different to selling differently.

#### 5. Details and motion

Hover states, transitions, icon style and the way the cart opens are small individually. Together they are what makes a store feel crafted rather than configured.

#### 6. Copy that sounds like you

"Free shipping on orders over $50" and "Shop the collection" appear on half the internet. Microcopy written in your brand's voice is one of the quickest ways to stand apart, and it costs nothing in performance.

Try the squint test

Take a screenshot of your homepage, cover the logo and blur it slightly. If a regular customer could not tell it was your store, neither can a new one, and the design is not doing its job.

### Theme, customised theme or custom build?

There are three honest routes, and each one is right for somebody.

- An off-the-shelf theme. Quickest and cheapest. Good for testing a product or launching on a tight budget. Expect your store to look like the theme's demo, because that is what it is.
- A customised premium theme. Colours, fonts and a few sections adjusted. A clear step up, but the underlying structure stays the same as every other store on that theme, and heavy customisation often means fighting the theme rather than building on it.
- A custom Shopify build. Designed from wireframes up around your brand and coded specifically for your catalogue. Costs more up front, and it is the only route where looking different is guaranteed rather than hoped for.

If you are still validating whether a product sells at all, a good theme is a sensible place to start. Once the brand is proven and you are spending real money to bring people to the store, the storefront becomes a growth asset, and a template stops being a saving.

### Will a unique design slow the store down or make it harder to edit?

It should do neither, and if a developer suggests otherwise, keep asking questions.

Hand-written code is usually lighter than a multipurpose theme, because it only contains what your store uses. Big themes ship features for every possible kind of shop, and stores built on them then add apps on top to fill the gaps. A custom build skips most of that weight, which helps load times and Core Web Vitals.

Editability depends on how the store is built, not on whether it is custom. A store built on Online Store 2.0 with every section exposed in the theme editor lets you change wording, images, colours and buttons yourself, and add new pages from the same building blocks, without touching code.

### How we make sure your store looks like no one else's

On our custom Shopify store development projects, distinctiveness is not a finishing touch. It is built into the process from the first week:

- 1Discovery starts with your brand, buyers and competitors, so we know what your store needs to look different from before anything is drawn.
- 2Wireframes come from your catalogue and your customers, not a starter layout. Nothing gets coded until you have signed off the structure and the visual design.
- 3Nothing is reused between clients. Every piece of Liquid, CSS and JavaScript is written for your store, so the finished storefront belongs to your brand alone.
- 4Every section is editable in the theme editor, so the store stays yours to run, and stays distinctive as you add products and pages.

### Questions to ask any Shopify developer before you hire

Whoever you work with, these five questions will tell you quickly whether you are buying a design or a theme with your logo on it.

- 1Do you start from a theme or from wireframes? If from a theme, which one, and how many of your other clients are on it?
- 2Can I see two stores you built and tell which is which without the logos?
- 3Which parts of the store will I be able to edit myself in the theme editor?
- 4Which apps do you expect the store to need, and what will each one add to load time?
- 5Who owns the code once the project is finished?

A theme gets you a store that works. A custom build gets you a store that people remember. Only one of those makes the next sale cheaper.

If your store looks like everybody else's and you want that to change, tell us what you sell and where you want the brand to go. You will get a plan, a fixed price and a launch date before any work starts.

# Revenue Systems vs Marketing Campaigns | Sushant Rana

URL: https://sushantrana.com/blog/revenue-systems-vs-marketing-campaigns/

Campaigns end. Systems compound. The structural difference between businesses that grow predictably and businesses that buy growth one month at a time.

- Home
- Blog
- Revenue Systems vs Marketing Campaigns: Why One Compounds and the Other Expires

Business Strategy · 18 Jun 2026 · 4 min read

## Revenue Systems vs Marketing Campaigns: Why One Compounds and the Other Expires

Campaigns end. Systems compound. The structural difference between businesses that grow predictably and businesses that buy growth one month at a time.

[Image: Revenue Systems vs Marketing Campaigns: Why One Compounds and the Other Expires]

In this article

- 01 What actually separates the two
- 02 The four layers a revenue system needs
- 03 How to tell which one you have
- 04 The uncomfortable part

Most businesses I meet do not have a marketing problem. They have a structure problem that shows up as a marketing problem. Spend goes in, leads come out, and when the spend stops, everything stops with it. Nothing that was built last quarter makes this quarter cheaper.

That is the difference between a campaign and a system. A campaign is a purchase. A system is an asset. Both can produce revenue this month; only one of them produces it more cheaply next month.

### What actually separates the two

The distinction is not budget size or channel choice. I have seen ₹50,000-a-month accounts that behave like systems and ₹50-lakh accounts that behave like a series of disconnected campaigns. What separates them is whether each month's work leaves behind something the next month can use.

- A campaign optimises for the period. It is judged on the spend and return inside a date range. When the range closes, the learning usually closes with it.
- A system optimises for the next period. Every month it hands forward cleaner data, a better-qualified audience, sharper creative, and a shorter path from click to cash.
- A campaign's cost is flat or rising. You pay the same auction price to reach the same stranger, forever.
- A system's cost curve bends down. Retargeting pools grow, the CRM learns which leads close, and organic and email start absorbing demand that used to cost money.

### The four layers a revenue system needs

When I audit an account, I am not really looking at the ads. I am looking for which of these four layers is missing, because growth stalls at the weakest one — not the loudest one.

#### 1. Strategy: the offer and who it is for

No amount of media buying fixes an offer that a buyer does not want at the price you are asking. Before I touch a campaign I want one sentence: who is this for, what changes for them, and why you rather than the alternative. If that sentence is vague, the ads will be vague and the auction will charge you for the vagueness.

#### 2. Acquisition: paid, organic, and the overlap

This is the layer everyone treats as the whole job. It is one quarter of it. Its real function in a system is not to generate leads — it is to generate qualified, attributable leads that the next two layers can act on.

#### 3. Tracking: knowing what actually happened

This is where most businesses are quietly broken. If your platform reports 200 conversions and your CRM shows 40 real conversations, you are optimising toward a number that does not exist. Every bid strategy, every budget decision, every creative test downstream of bad tracking is a guess wearing a suit.

The cheapest fix in marketing

Before increasing budget, reconcile one month of platform conversions against your CRM. In most accounts I open, the gap is 30-60%. Closing it changes what the algorithm learns — and that is free performance.

#### 4. Conversion: what happens after the lead arrives

A lead that waits nine hours for a first response is a different asset from one contacted in five minutes. The follow-up sequence, the routing rules, the reminder before the call — these are marketing, even though nobody in marketing owns them. They are also the parts that compound fastest, because they cost nothing per additional lead.

### How to tell which one you have

Ask four questions. Honest answers take about ten minutes and tell you more than a month of reporting.

- 1If you paused all paid spend for 30 days, how much revenue would still arrive? If the answer is close to zero, you have campaigns.
- 2Is your cost per qualified lead lower than it was six months ago? If it is flat, nothing is compounding.
- 3Can you name your close rate by source? If not, you are optimising volume, not revenue.
- 4What did last quarter build that this quarter inherits? If the honest answer is 'nothing', that is the finding.

### The uncomfortable part

Systems are slower to show results. A campaign can show a return in week one. A system often looks worse in month one, because you spend it fixing tracking, rewriting the offer, and building follow-up that nobody sees. Month four is where the two lines cross, and month twelve is where the gap stops being an argument.

You can rent demand or you can build the machine that captures it. Renting is faster. Building is cheaper every month after the first.

If you are choosing between the two, the deciding question is not which produces more revenue this quarter. It is how many more quarters you intend to be in business.

# Lead Quality Over Lead Volume | Sushant Rana

URL: https://sushantrana.com/blog/lead-quality-over-lead-volume/

A thousand leads that never answer the phone cost more than a hundred that do. How to rebuild campaigns around qualified conversations instead of form fills.

- Home
- Blog
- Lead Quality Over Lead Volume: The Metric Shift That Changes Everything

Marketing · 4 Jun 2026 · 4 min read

## Lead Quality Over Lead Volume: The Metric Shift That Changes Everything

A thousand leads that never answer the phone cost more than a hundred that do. How to rebuild campaigns around qualified conversations instead of form fills.

[Image: Lead Quality Over Lead Volume: The Metric Shift That Changes Everything]

In this article

- 01 The arithmetic nobody runs
- 02 Why platforms drift toward volume
- 03 Rebuilding around qualified conversations
- 04 The metric to put on the wall

Cost per lead is the most reassuring bad metric in marketing. It always improves when you ask it to. Widen the targeting, soften the form, add a discount hook — the number falls, the dashboard turns green, and the sales team quietly stops trusting marketing.

The problem is not that CPL is wrong. It is that CPL is a cost metric being used as a quality metric, and those move in opposite directions more often than anyone admits.

### The arithmetic nobody runs

Two campaigns, same monthly spend. Campaign A produces 500 leads at a low CPL. Campaign B produces 120 at four times the CPL. On the dashboard, A wins decisively.

Now add the two columns nobody puts on the dashboard: what share of each set answers the phone, and what share of those closes. When A's leads connect at 20% and close at 5%, and B's connect at 65% and close at 18%, B produces roughly three times the customers for the same money — and it looked like the loser all quarter.

Run this on your own numbers

Take last quarter by source: leads, connect rate, close rate, average deal value. Multiply them out to cost per customer. The ranking almost never matches the cost-per-lead ranking, and that mismatch is the whole argument.

There is also a cost that never appears anywhere: your sales team's hours. Four hundred unqualified leads is not free — it is a week of somebody's month spent being ignored, plus the morale cost of a pipeline that mostly does not answer.

### Why platforms drift toward volume

Not malice — instruction. If you hand Google or Meta a 'lead' conversion that fires on form submit, you have told the algorithm that all form submits are equally valuable. It will then do exactly what you asked, extremely well: find you the cheapest people who will fill in a form. Cheap form-fillers are not the same population as buyers.

The algorithm is not the problem. The definition you gave it is.

### Rebuilding around qualified conversations

#### Move the conversion event down the funnel

Stop optimising to form submit. Optimise to the first event that correlates with revenue — a held sales call, a qualified status in the CRM, a completed application. Send that event back to the platform with offline conversion imports or the conversions API. This single change does more for lead quality than any targeting adjustment.

- Qualified lead — meets your basic fit criteria (budget, geography, category). The minimum viable upgrade over raw form fills.
- Connected conversation — someone actually spoke to them. Strong signal, arrives within days.
- Closed revenue with value — the real target. Best signal, but slow; use it once volume supports it.

#### Add friction on purpose

Every field you remove raises volume and lowers intent. That trade is sometimes right — and it is a trade, not a free win. Adding budget range, timeline, or a required phone number will cut your lead count and raise your customer count. Do it deliberately, and measure it at the customer line, not the lead line.

#### Let the copy disqualify

Ads that state price bands, minimum engagement size, or who this is not for will lose you clicks you were going to lose anyway — after you paid for them. Pre-qualifying in the ad is the cheapest filter available.

#### Feed the negative signal back

Junk leads are training data. Push your disqualified list back as an exclusion audience and let the platform learn the shape of a bad lead, not just the shape of a good one. Most accounts do the first half of this and never the second.

### The metric to put on the wall

Replace cost per lead with cost per qualified conversation, and review it by source. It is harder to calculate, it moves slower, and it will occasionally make a campaign you like look bad. That is precisely why it is worth having.

Volume is what you report when you cannot yet measure quality. Once you can, nobody asks about volume again.

# Practical AI Automation Without a Data Team | Sushant Rana

URL: https://sushantrana.com/blog/practical-ai-automation-without-a-data-team/

You don't need ML engineers. You need five workflows: lead scoring, follow-up, reporting, routing, and reactivation — built on the CRM you already pay for.

- Home
- Blog
- Practical AI Automation for Businesses That Don't Have a Data Team

AI · 21 May 2026 · 4 min read

## Practical AI Automation for Businesses That Don't Have a Data Team

You don't need ML engineers. You need five workflows: lead scoring, follow-up, reporting, routing, and reactivation — built on the CRM you already pay for.

[Image: Practical AI Automation for Businesses That Don't Have a Data Team]

In this article

- 01 1. Lead scoring that runs before anyone opens the CRM
- 02 2. Follow-up that does not depend on someone remembering
- 03 3. Reporting that assembles itself
- 04 4. Routing that matches the lead to the right person
- 05 5. Reactivation of the list you already own
- 06 What to build first

Almost every 'AI strategy' I am shown by a mid-sized business is a list of tools. Almost every one that works is a list of decisions that used to wait for a human and no longer do. The tools are interchangeable. The decisions are the asset.

You do not need a data team for any of what follows. You need the CRM you are already paying for, a workflow tool, and the discipline to build one of these at a time.

### 1. Lead scoring that runs before anyone opens the CRM

The highest-value minute in your business is the one right after a lead arrives, and it is usually spent on whoever happens to be at the top of a list. Scoring fixes the ordering.

Start rules-based, not clever: company size, geography, stated budget, the page they converted on, the service they picked. That alone reorders the queue usefully. Once you have a few hundred closed-won and closed-lost records, let a model weight those same fields — it will find combinations your rules missed. Do not start there; you will be modelling noise.

Order of operations

Rules first, model second. A rules-based score you trust beats a model you cannot explain to the person who has to act on it at 9am.

### 2. Follow-up that does not depend on someone remembering

Speed to first contact is the most reliably underexploited lever in lead generation, and it is entirely an operations problem. An instant, personal-sounding acknowledgement, a reminder before the call, a nudge after a no-show, and a sequence that stops the moment a human replies.

Where AI genuinely helps is drafting the message with the lead's own context — their industry, the page they came from, the service they selected — so the third follow-up does not read like the first one resent. Where it does not help is deciding to send it. That is a workflow rule, and rules are more reliable than judgement here.

### 3. Reporting that assembles itself

If a person spends the first two days of each month rebuilding the same spreadsheet, you are paying a salary for copy and paste. Pull spend from the ad platforms, outcomes from the CRM, join them on a campaign ID you control, and have the summary waiting on Monday.

The AI part is the last inch: a short written read of what changed and what looks anomalous. Useful, but only once the numbers underneath are trustworthy. Automating a report built on broken tracking just distributes the error faster.

### 4. Routing that matches the lead to the right person

Round-robin is fair to your team and expensive for you. Route by territory, by service, by deal size, by language — and set an escalation so a high-score lead that sits untouched for an hour goes to someone else automatically. That last rule usually pays for the entire build.

### 5. Reactivation of the list you already own

Every business I work with is sitting on a few thousand contacts who did not buy and were never contacted again. This is the cheapest revenue in the building — you paid to acquire them once already.

- Segment on why they went cold: no budget then, wrong timing, lost to a competitor, simply never answered.
- Send a reason to come back that matches the segment — not a generic newsletter.
- Score the replies and push the warm ones straight into the pipeline with a task attached.

### What to build first

Not all five. Pick the one where the delay currently costs you the most money — for most businesses that is follow-up speed — and ship it in a fortnight. Measure it for a month. Then build the next.

Automation does not fix a broken process. It runs the broken process faster and at greater volume. Fix the decision first, then automate it.

The businesses that get value from AI are not the ones with the best models. They are the ones that were honest about which decisions were being made badly, and automated those.

# Privacy Policy | Sushant Rana, Business Growth Consultant

## Privacy Policy

What sushantrana.com collects when you submit an enquiry, who processes it, how long it is kept, and how to have it corrected or deleted.

Last updated 11 Aug 2026

This policy explains what personal information sushantrana.com collects, why it is collected, who processes it, and what you can ask me to do with it. It covers this website only — not the separate agreements or tools used inside a paid engagement, which are dealt with in that engagement's own contract.

### Who is responsible for your data

This site is operated by Sushant Rana, an independent business growth consultant trading as a sole proprietor in Chandigarh, India. For the purposes of Indian data protection law I am the person who decides why and how your information is used, and I am the point of contact for any question about it.

You can reach me about anything in this policy at me@sushantrana.com.

### What I collect

#### Information you give me

When you submit the enquiry or consultation form on this site, I collect the fields you fill in:

- Name, email address and phone number — required, so I can reply to you.
- Business or website — optional context about who you are.
- The service you selected and whether you want a free consultation or a service enquiry — so your enquiry reaches me already understood.
- Your message — optional, and entirely up to you what it contains.

Please do not put sensitive personal information, financial account details, passwords or client data into the message box. It is a contact form, not a secure channel.

#### Information collected automatically

Alongside a form submission I record the page you submitted from, the referring URL, and your browser's user-agent string. This tells me which page produced an enquiry so I know what to write more of. Your IP address is used momentarily to rate-limit the form against spam; it is not written to the database.

Separately, my hosting provider keeps standard server logs (including IP addresses) as part of running and securing the site.

### Cookies and analytics

This site loads Google Tag Manager, which in turn may load analytics and advertising tags such as Google Analytics and advertising platform pixels. These set cookies or similar identifiers in your browser and are used to understand how the site is used and to measure marketing performance.

- Strictly necessary — needed to serve the site and keep the form working. These cannot be switched off.
- Analytics — how many people visit, which pages they read, how they arrived.
- Advertising / measurement — attributing an enquiry back to a campaign, and building remarketing audiences.

You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings at any time; the site will still work. You can also opt out of Google Analytics specifically using Google's browser add-on.

### Why I use it, and on what basis

- To answer your enquiry and arrange a call — because you asked me to, by submitting the form.
- To follow up about the service you selected — my legitimate interest in responding to a business enquiry, and steps taken at your request before entering a contract.
- To keep the site secure and working — legitimate interest in preventing spam and abuse.
- To measure marketing performance — legitimate interest in knowing which pages and campaigns produce enquiries, and consent where the law requires it for cookies.

I do not sell your personal information, and I do not add you to a marketing mailing list from the enquiry form without asking you first.

### Who processes your data

I run a small practice and use established providers rather than building my own infrastructure. Each of these acts as a processor on my instructions:

- Supabase — stores enquiry submissions in a private database that is not readable from the browser.
- Resend — delivers the notification email that tells me an enquiry has arrived.
- Hostinger — hosts the website and keeps server logs.
- Google (Tag Manager, Analytics, Ads) — analytics and campaign measurement, as described above.

Beyond these, I share your information only where I am legally required to, or where you have asked me to.

### Where your data is held

These providers operate globally, so your information may be stored or processed outside India, including in the United States and the European Union. Where that happens I rely on the provider's own contractual safeguards for international transfers.

### How long I keep it

Enquiries are kept for a maximum of three weeks from our last contact, after which they are deleted. Records connected to a paid engagement are kept separately, for as long as tax and accounting law requires. You can ask me to delete your enquiry sooner at any time.

### Your rights

You can ask me to:

- Tell you what I hold about you, and where it came from.
- Correct anything that is wrong or out of date.
- Delete your information, where I have no ongoing legal or contractual reason to keep it.
- Withdraw consent to marketing or analytics cookies.
- Object to or restrict a particular use of your information.

Email me@sushantrana.com and I will respond within 30 days. If you are in India and you are not satisfied with how I have handled your request, you may complain to the Data Protection Board of India. If you are in the UK or EU, you may complain to your national supervisory authority.

### Security

The site is served over HTTPS. Enquiries are written to a database that the public website key cannot read from — it can only add new rows — so a leaked browser key could not be used to download enquiries. No system is perfectly secure, and I cannot guarantee the security of information while it is in transit to me.

### Children

This is a business-to-business site and is not directed at children. I do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 18. If you believe a child has submitted information through this site, email me and I will delete it.

### Links to other sites

This site links to third-party websites and platforms. Once you follow such a link, this policy no longer applies — the destination site has its own, and I am not responsible for it.

### Changes to this policy

If I change how the site handles personal information, I will update this page and the date at the top. Material changes will be reflected here before the change takes effect.

### Contact

Questions, corrections or deletion requests — email me@sushantrana.com and put "Privacy" in the subject line so it reaches me quickly.

The basics

### What Amazon PPC is and why it matters

Amazon PPC, or pay per click advertising, lets you pay to place your products at the top of Amazon search results and on product pages. You only pay when a shopper clicks your ad.

This matters because Amazon is where people go when they are ready to buy, not just browse. Good ads put your product in front of these buyers, win sales, and even help push your product higher in the free organic results over time.

The number that matters

### Understanding ACoS and TACoS for real profit

ACoS, or advertising cost of sale, is the share of your ad sales that you spend on ads. A lower ACoS means more profit from each ad sale, so I work hard to keep it healthy for your margins.

TACoS, or total advertising cost of sale, looks at your ad spend against your total sales, including organic. This is the bigger picture number I watch to make sure your ads are truly growing your whole business, not just shifting sales around.

ACoS

Ad spend ÷ ad sales

Lower means more profit from each ad sale.

TACoS

Ad spend ÷ total sales

Includes organic sales. The bigger picture number.

I have never added negative keywords Wasteful clicks on searches that do not convert push your ACoS up. I only run automatic campaigns The winners never move into manual campaigns with proper bid control. My campaign structure is messy A clean structure is the key to a low ACoS. My listing has weak titles, images or few reviews Even the best ads struggle when the listing is weak. I look at ACoS but never at TACoS TACoS shows whether ads grow the whole business.

Common questions

### Amazon PPC questions, answered

ACoS, targeting, listings and reporting. If yours is not here, ask me on the call.

#### What is Amazon PPC?

Amazon PPC is pay per click advertising on Amazon. You pay only when a shopper clicks your ad, and your products get shown at the top of search results and on product pages where buyers can see them.

#### What is ACoS?

ACoS stands for advertising cost of sale. It is the share of your ad sales that you spend on ads. A lower ACoS means you keep more profit from every ad sale.

#### How much budget do I need for Amazon ads?

It depends on your products, your competition and your goals. Some sellers start small and scale up once we find profitable keywords. On our call I will suggest a realistic starting budget.

#### What is the difference between Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands?

Sponsored Products promote a single product and drive most ad sales. Sponsored Brands show your logo and several products at the top of search and are great for brand awareness.

#### Do you optimize my product listings too?

I review your listings and give clear advice on titles, images and content, because even the best ads struggle if the listing is weak. A strong listing plus good ads is what really grows sales.

#### What is the difference between keyword and product targeting?

Keyword targeting shows your ad when people search certain words. Product targeting places your ad on specific product pages and categories, often your competitors', to win shoppers who are comparing.

#### How soon will I see results?

You can see clicks and sales within the first few days. The first few weeks are used to gather data and cut waste, so a lower ACoS and steady sales usually build from the first month.

#### Can you lower my ACoS?

Yes, this is a big part of my job. I do it by adding negative keywords, adjusting bids, improving campaign structure and moving budget to what actually sells.

#### What is the difference between automatic and manual campaigns?

Automatic campaigns let Amazon find keywords for you and are great for discovery. Manual campaigns give you full control over bids and targeting, which is where the real optimization happens.

#### What are negative keywords?

Negative keywords are searches you do not want to pay for. Adding them stops wasted clicks and lowers your ACoS, which protects your budget.

#### Do Amazon ads help my organic ranking?

Yes. More ad sales send a positive signal to Amazon, which can lift your product in the free search results over time. So your ads help even after they stop.

#### What reports will I get?

You get clear monthly reports showing sales, spend, ACoS, TACoS and your best products, plus updates whenever something important changes.

#### Can you work with sellers outside India?

Yes. I work with Amazon sellers in the US, Canada and other marketplaces, and I can manage your account from anywhere.

#### Can you fix my existing Amazon ad account?

Yes. This is a common request. I audit your account, find the waste and rebuild the structure so your ads become profitable again.

#### Do I need good reviews and a strong listing first?

It helps a lot. Ads bring shoppers, but reviews and a clear listing help turn those clicks into sales. I will point out what to fix first so your ad budget is not wasted.

#### How do I get started?

Just book a free Amazon Ads audit using the button on this page. I will review your account and show you how we can grow your sales and lower your ACoS.

### Ready to sell more on Amazon?

Let us look at your products and your ad account together and build a plan that grows profitable sales. The first step is a simple, friendly call.

The challenge

### The special problems of ecommerce SEO and how I solve them

Online stores face SEO problems that normal websites do not. You often have thin or duplicate product descriptions, hundreds of similar pages, filters that create endless URLs, and out of stock products that lose their rankings.

I know how to handle all of these. I write unique content where it matters, control the filter and duplicate page issues, and manage out of stock pages so you do not lose the rankings you worked hard to earn. Solving these problems is what separates real ecommerce SEO from basic SEO.

- Unique content where it matters
- Filter and duplicate pages under control
- Out of stock pages that keep their rankings

Store check Self check

Tick everything that sounds like your online store.

My product descriptions are copied from the supplier Thin or duplicate descriptions make product pages hard to rank. My category pages are just a grid of products Category pages are often your biggest ranking opportunity. My filters create a new URL for every color, size and sort Endless filter URLs confuse Google and waste crawl budget. Out of stock products disappear or show an error Handled wrongly, they lose rankings you worked hard to earn. I have many near identical product pages Similar pages compete with each other for the same searches. My listings show no stars or details in search Product schema and reviews help your listings stand out.

Common questions

### Ecommerce SEO questions, answered

Products, categories, filters and reporting. If yours is not here, ask me on the call.

#### What is ecommerce SEO?

Ecommerce SEO is the work that helps your online store rank on Google for buying searches. It focuses on your product pages, category pages and the technical health of your store.

#### How is ecommerce SEO different from normal SEO?

Ecommerce SEO deals with special problems like hundreds of product pages, duplicate content, filters and out of stock items. It also puts a big focus on category and product pages that capture buyers.

#### Do I need SEO if I already run paid ads?

Yes. Ads stop when you stop paying, but SEO keeps bringing buyers for free. Using both together usually lowers your overall cost of getting a sale.

#### Should I optimize category pages or product pages?

Both, but category pages are often the biggest opportunity because they target broad buying searches. I optimize both in the right order for the best gains.

#### What about duplicate product descriptions?

Duplicate descriptions can hurt your rankings. I write unique content for your most important products and handle the rest in a smart way to avoid problems.

#### How do you handle out of stock products?

Out of stock pages can lose valuable rankings if handled wrongly. I manage them so you keep the ranking power and guide shoppers to related products.

#### What is the faceted navigation problem?

Filters on stores can create endless duplicate URLs that confuse Google and waste crawl budget. I control these so your important pages get the attention instead.

#### How soon will I see results?

Ecommerce SEO usually shows movement over two to three months, with bigger gains building over time as your pages gain authority.

#### Do reviews help ecommerce SEO?

Yes. Reviews add fresh content and trust, and with review schema your listings can show stars in search, which lifts clicks and sales.

#### Can you do SEO for my Shopify store?

Yes. I work with Shopify, WooCommerce and other platforms and know the SEO strengths and limits of each one.

#### Will you write product descriptions?

I write or improve descriptions for your most important products so they are unique and helpful, which supports both rankings and sales.

#### How do you find product keywords?

I research the exact words shoppers use before buying, including brand, model and buying phrases, and map them to the right pages.

#### Can ecommerce SEO reduce my ad costs?

Yes. As your organic sales grow, you can rely less on ads for the same revenue, which lowers your overall cost of getting a sale.

#### Do you fix technical issues too?

Yes. Technical health is a big part of ecommerce SEO. I fix crawl, speed and duplicate content issues that hold stores back.

#### What reports will I get?

You get clear monthly reports showing rankings, organic traffic and sales, plus updates on the work done.

The basics

### What email automation is and why it matters

Email automation is a set of emails that send themselves based on what a person does, such as signing up, buying, or leaving items in a cart. Once it is built, it runs around the clock without you touching it.

The basics

### What enterprise SEO is and why it is different

Enterprise SEO is SEO for large websites, usually those with thousands or even millions of pages, many teams and complex systems. It is not just bigger SEO, it is a different way of working.

On a large site you cannot fix pages one by one. You have to work at the template level, plan at scale and work with several teams to get changes live. Done right, the results can be huge because every improvement is multiplied across many pages.

- Work at the template level
- Plans built for scale
- Changes live with your teams
Book your free enterprise SEO consultation

One fix, two ways Example

Every page built on your product template

One page improved. Every other page on the template keeps the problem.

Why it is different

### Why large websites need a special SEO approach

Size changes the rules. What works page by page on a small site does not work across thousands of pages.

#### Scale changes everything

With thousands of pages, small mistakes repeat across the whole site and small wins multiply. The focus shifts from single pages to patterns and templates.

#### More technical complexity

Large sites have crawl budget limits, complex code and many moving parts. Technical SEO becomes far more important and more challenging.

#### Many stakeholders and approvals

Changes often need sign off from several teams. Part of my job is making SEO easy to understand and approve, so good ideas actually get live.

#### Template level impact

Fixing one page template can improve thousands of pages instantly. This is the biggest advantage of enterprise SEO when it is done well.

What I do

### The enterprise SEO work I do for you

Six parts of SEO planned for the size of your site. Pick one to see what it looks like.

Site-wide technical fixes Example

- /search?q= pages Crawled, but worth nothing Blocked
- /products/*?sort= Endless filter URLs Controlled
- Article template Slow to load on every article Faster
- /old-section/ Pages no longer linked Reconnected

Crawl budget goes to the pages that earn traffic.

Large scale technical SEO. I fix crawl budget, indexing, speed and structure issues at the level that affects your whole site, not just a few pages.

The advantage

### Why one fix can improve thousands of pages

The real power of enterprise SEO is leverage. On a small site, fixing a title tag helps one page. On a large site, fixing a title tag in a template can help thousands of pages in a single change.

This is why I focus on finding the patterns and template level issues that hold back your whole site. The right fix here can bring a jump in traffic that no amount of single page work could match.

- Patterns found across the whole site
- Template issues fixed once
- Every page on the template lifted

Scale check Self check

Common questions

### Enterprise SEO questions, answered

Scale, templates, teams and reporting. If yours is not here, ask me on the call.

#### What is enterprise SEO?

Enterprise SEO is SEO for large websites with thousands of pages, many teams and complex systems. It focuses on template level and pattern level work rather than fixing pages one by one.

#### How is enterprise SEO different from normal SEO?

Normal SEO often fixes single pages. Enterprise SEO works at scale, where one template fix can improve thousands of pages, and where technical complexity and team approvals matter much more.

#### What counts as a large website?

There is no exact line, but sites with thousands of pages, large catalogs or lots of content usually need an enterprise approach because their scale changes how SEO works.

#### Why does scale change SEO so much?

At scale, small mistakes repeat across the whole site and small wins multiply. The focus moves from individual pages to the patterns and templates behind them.

#### What are template level fixes?

A template is the design used by many pages, like all product pages or all articles. Fixing SEO issues in a template improves every page that uses it in one change.

#### How do you handle thousands of pages?

I focus on the patterns and templates that affect the most pages, and on technical issues like crawl budget and indexing, so my work scales across your whole site.

#### Do you work with our in-house team?

Yes. Enterprise SEO needs teamwork. I work with your marketing, content and development teams, and I make changes easy to understand and approve.

#### How long does it take to see results?

Enterprise sites can see meaningful gains within a few months once template and technical fixes go live, and results keep growing as the strategy rolls out.

#### Can you handle multiple locations or languages?

Yes. I can plan and manage SEO for multi location and multi language sites, including the technical setup that helps each version rank in the right place.

#### How do you report to management?

I create clear reports that show traffic, rankings and business impact in language that both marketing teams and senior leaders can act on.

#### What tools do you use?

I use enterprise grade crawlers, Google Search Console and analytics tools, but the real value is in knowing which large scale fixes actually move the needle.

#### Can you fix a big site that lost traffic?

Yes. Large sites often lose traffic due to template or technical issues. I find the cause, fix it at scale and work to recover your rankings.

#### Do you do the work or just advise?

Both. I create the strategy and roadmap and work hands on with your teams to get the changes live, rather than just handing over a report.

#### What is a Google Business Profile?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your business on Google Maps and in the local pack. It shows your details, photos, reviews and more, and it drives local calls and visits.

#### Is Google Business Profile the same as Google My Business?

Yes. Google My Business is the old name. Google renamed it to Google Business Profile, but many people still call it GMB. It is the same free listing.

#### Is a Google Business Profile free?

Yes, the profile itself is completely free. My service is about optimizing and managing it so it actually brings you customers, which most free profiles fail to do.

It helps people find you on the map, read your reviews, call you and get directions. A strong profile can bring a steady flow of local customers with no ad cost.

#### How do I get my profile verified?

Google verifies your business through methods like a postcard, phone, email or video. I guide you through the process so your profile goes live correctly.

#### How important are reviews for my profile?

Very important. Reviews build trust with customers and help your ranking. I set up a simple system to get more genuine reviews and to respond to them.

#### Can you optimize my existing profile?

Yes. Most profiles are only half set up. I complete and optimize every part so it ranks better and attracts more customers.

#### What are Google posts?

Google posts are short updates you can add to your profile, like offers or news. They keep your profile active, which Google and customers both like.

#### How soon will I see results?

You often see more calls and clicks within a few weeks of proper optimization, with stronger map rankings building over a couple of months.

#### Do I need a website to use a Google Business Profile?

No, but a website helps a lot. Even without one, a strong profile can bring calls and visits. I will advise the best path for your situation.

#### What categories should I choose?

The right categories help Google show you for the correct searches. I research and pick the best primary and extra categories for your business.

Why it works

### Why Google Shopping Ads are great for ecommerce

Shopping puts the product itself in front of the shopper. Here is why that works so well for online stores.

#### Your products are seen, not just read

Shopping Ads show a real photo of your product. People shop with their eyes, so a clear image gets far more attention than a plain text ad.

#### High buyer intent

Shopping Ads appear when people are searching for a product to buy. These are warm shoppers who are close to a purchase.

#### The price is shown upfront

Because the price is visible before the click, the people who click are already comfortable with your pricing. This means better quality clicks and less wasted spend.

#### Strong return for online stores

When the feed and campaigns are set up well, Shopping often gives one of the best returns on ad spend for ecommerce.

Standard Shopping. Classic Shopping campaigns that give you full control over which products show and how much you bid.

Best for careful, hands on management.

How it works

### How Google Shopping actually works

Shopping Ads do not use keywords the way Search Ads do. Instead, Google reads your product feed, which is a file that lists all your products with their titles, images, prices and details. Google then decides which searches to show your products for, based on that feed.

This is why the feed is the real engine behind Shopping. A clean, well written feed leads to better placement and cheaper sales. A messy feed holds your whole account back, no matter how much you spend.

- No keywords, the feed decides
- Titles, images, prices and details
- A clean feed means better placement

One product in your feed Example

- Title Brand, product and key feature Clear
- Product type The right category Correct
- Image Clear photo on a clean background Strong
- Details Size, colour and material filled in Complete

Google understands the product, and matches it to the right searches.

The secret

### Why the product feed is the most important part

Most Shopping accounts fail because of a weak product feed, not a weak budget. If your product titles are unclear or your images are poor, Google shows your products for the wrong searches and your sales suffer.

I spend real time getting your feed right. This means clear, keyword rich titles, correct product types, strong images and complete details. A strong feed is the single biggest thing that lifts your Shopping results.
